items.title: From lectern to bench: Why law professors belong in India’s higher judiciary
items.summary: Teaching law is a lifelong apprenticeship and that is the premise of this blog: law professors, who live inside legal developments every day deserve a real place among those considered for the higher judiciary. The framers of our Constitution agreed. Article 124(3)(c) makes a citizen eligible for the Supreme Court if he or she is, in the opinion of the President, "a distinguished jurist". Yet, in more than 76 years, not a single jurist has entered the Court through this door. The High Courts have no such door at all, since Article 217(2) admits only those with 10 years of judicial office or 10 years at the Bar. The silence has now been broken from within the Court itself. On August 30, 2026, addressing the LL.M. convocation of National Law University, Delhi, Justice Ujjal Bhuyan called the clause one of the Constitution’s "unused mandates" . He dismissed the objection that scholars lack courtroom experience as shallow, pointing to academics who serve on constitutional courts in the United States, the United Kingdom, Canada and Kenya.
